rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

positions.catalyst: TUESDAY 9/15 -- US EQUITY MARKET OPEN, PRE-MARKET RUN AT 05:40 CT. THE CATALYST IS A THREE-YEAR CEILING BREAKING ON THE LONG END OF THE TREASURY CURVE, AND IT IS STILL BREAKING AS I WRITE THIS. The benchmark US 10-year yield broke through 5.00% yesterday for the first time since 2023, touching 5.02% -- reported as the highest level since 2007 -- driven by expanding term premia and persistent energy inflation. That is not a closed event. The selloff is CONTINUING in this morning's book: TLT 80.93 close against an 80.61 bid (-0.40%), TMF (3x long bond) 29.42 against 29.03 (-1.2%), TMV 44.55 against 45.05/45.12 (+1.2%). Bonds are being sold at 05:40 CT, after the round number already gave way. THE DRIVERS ALL PUSH THE SAME DIRECTION INSIDE MY WINDOW. Brent is $107.30 with the Saudi East-West pipeline still offline and Reuters sources putting repairs at five to six weeks; diesel printed an all-time high. August CPI came in +0.4% headline with core +0.3% faster than expected, and August PPI +0.4% m/m and +5.4% y/y. The FOMC decides tomorrow, Wednesday 16 September at 2:00pm ET, with the market-implied probability of a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% now at 91% under Chair Warsh after his hawkish Jackson Hole speech. Every one of those inputs is a reason for the long end to keep cheapening across today's session. THE CONFIRMING TELL IS WHAT IS *NOT* HAPPENING. Gold is not bid: GLD 392.84 close against 391.99/392.10, roughly -0.2%. NUGT flat to -0.6%. UUP flat. If this were a fear-driven flight out of risk, gold would be catching a bid and would be the asset rescuing Treasuries. It is not. That tells me this is a real-rate and term-premium repricing rather than a risk-off episode -- and a term-premium move does not attract the safe-haven duration bid that would be the main thing capable of reversing it inside 24 hours. CLOSED GUSH AT 47.20 FOR -$580.52 (-5.60%). I WAS WRONG IN EXACTLY THE WAY I WROTE DOWN THAT I MIGHT BE, AND THE PRE-COMMITMENT I MADE IS NOW BINDING. Yesterday's entry named as the primary risk that I was 'buying an oil spike that is already nine percent old' and that geopolitical premia are 'fully priced within 48 hours of the headline and then bleed out.' That is precisely what happened, and the de-escalation headline I said had no scheduled venue to emerge from emerged anyway: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the pipeline should be back online 'soon.' Crude did NOT break -- Brent closed above $105 and is $107.30 now -- and GUSH still fell 5.6%. That is the exact condition I pre-committed to: 'if GUSH is stopped out or the oil premium visibly bleeds while crude holds above $105, that is evidence the geopolitical premium is already fully priced, and I should not re-enter a second oil trade on the same headline a day later.' The condition fired. GUSH, ERX, BNO, USO and XLE are therefore excluded today by rule, not by judgement, and I am recording that BNO -- the unlevered Brent expression I said I would own 'if my conviction were lower' -- is up only +0.4% pre-market, meaning the lower-leverage version of yesterday's trade would also have been a loser. The error was the thesis, not the leverage. Taking 2x instead of 3x saved money; it did not make the trade right. PRICE FEED INTEGRITY. The proxy is again stale for equities and live for crypto, the same signature logged on 9/13 and 9/14. Three pulls (asOf 10:40:35.285Z, 10:40:45.846Z, 10:44:50.014Z) show BTC-USD ticking 76,897.88 -> 76,903.72 while every equity symbol returns Monday's settled close unchanged: GUSH 47.20, TMV 44.55, TLT 80.93, UVXY 18.23, SOXS 51.73. Robinhood independently confirms 47.20 and 44.55 as the official sip-list-exchange 2026-09-14 closes, so the proxy is correct but carries no pre-market print. Mandated fallback to Robinhood real-time applies for the entry.
positions.driver: LONG TMV -- DIREXION DAILY 20+ YEAR TREASURY BEAR 3X -- 100% of capital, 216.888298 shares at 45.12, $9,786.00 deployed, stop 40.61 (-10%, the mandated 3x band). THE TRADE IS: BE SHORT DURATION WHILE THE LONG END IS ACTIVELY REPRICING THROUGH A LEVEL THAT HELD FOR THREE YEARS. Yields breaking 5% is the single variable that explains the rest of today's tape -- it is why semis are derating on a discount-rate basis, why the futures are heavy, and why gold cannot rally. Rather than trade a downstream consequence of the rates move, which is what I did badly yesterday with energy equities, I am trading the rates move itself. WHY THE LEVERAGE AND THE STOP ARE COMPATIBLE HERE AND WERE NOT ELSEWHERE -- THIS IS THE ACTUAL REASON I PICKED THIS INSTRUMENT. I pulled three months of daily bars and measured it instead of assuming. TMV's worst close-to-close day since 15 June is -4.9% (8/19, 43.60 -> 41.47); its best is +4.8% (7/29). Typical daily range is 2.5-3.4%. A -10% stop therefore sits at roughly TWO TIMES the worst day observed in a quarter, so ordinary noise cannot reach it -- only a genuine dovish shock can. Compare SOXL, whose last three months contain -17.0% (9/14), -16.6% (7/2) and -16.0% (7/29) days: a 3x semis fund with the same -10% band would be stopped out by a completely routine session. This is what 'highest risk/reward WITH the most downside protection' actually means in practice -- 3x on a low-realised-vol underlying carries roughly the position volatility of 1x on semis, and it is the best leverage-to-stop-distance ratio available to me today. I want to state plainly that this is a volatility-matched argument and NOT revenge sizing after yesterday's loss; I checked that motive specifically, and the test I applied was arithmetic on historical bars, not a need to make the money back. WHY THE PAYOFF IS ASYMMETRIC. A decisive break of a round number that has capped the 10-year for three years tends to produce mechanical follow-through, because convexity hedgers -- mortgage servicers and insurers whose liabilities extend as rates rise -- are forced to SELL duration into a selloff. That flow is non-discretionary and self-reinforcing, and it is the fat right tail. The left tail requires a bond rally, which needs either a dovish surprise (the FOMC, tomorrow at 2:00pm ET, strictly OUTSIDE my window, which closes at 06:30 CT Wednesday) or a flight-to-quality bid -- and gold's failure to rally is live evidence that the flight-to-quality bid is not currently present. ON NOT CHASING. TMV at 45.12 is +1.28% against Monday's 44.55 close, far inside the 8-10% no-chase band. It is near the top of its three-month range and made 45.32 intraday yesterday, so I am buying a breakout attempt rather than an extended move -- I note below that breakouts fail often, which is the honest cost of this entry. CHOSEN OVER, WITH THE COMPARATIVE ARGUMENT STATED: (a) SOXS, DIREXION DAILY SEMICONDUCTOR BEAR 3X -- the trade I rejected yesterday purely on the no-chase rule at +13.7%, and which today is priced at 50.79 ask against a 51.73 close, i.e. -1.8% and no longer extended. The thesis is real and durable: Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, SpaceXAI and Musk all endorsed slowing frontier development, the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 5.9% on Monday for its worst day since July, NVDA -3.4%, INTC -5.6%, MU -5.2%, SoftBank -11% in Tokyo. REJECTED FOR TWO SPECIFIC REASONS. First, the tape is directly contradicting it right now: SOXL is bid 103.01 against a 101.13 close (+1.86%), SMH +0.42%, NVDA +0.65%, and critically the epicentre memory names are ALL bouncing together -- MU +0.74%, SNDK +0.76%, WDC +0.76% -- while SPX futures are -0.5%. Semis are the only thing bid in a down tape, which is a day-two dip-buy reflex, and buying a 3x inverse into that is shorting into strength. Second and more decisive, the stop arithmetic above: a -10% band on SOXS is a 3.3% move in the SOX, which is well under one standard deviation for that index, so the position would be a coin flip on being stopped out regardless of whether the thesis is right. I still believe the AI-capex narrative shift is the most important durable story on the board; I just cannot express it at 3x with a stop that survives contact. (b) UVXY / VXX / VIXY, long volatility into the FOMC -- structurally the right window (vol bids INTO an event and crushes ON it, and my window ends before the event). Rejected on two counts: with the hike 91% priced there is little decision uncertainty left to bid, only guidance uncertainty which resolves tomorrow afternoon; and UVXY's own chart shows relentless contango bleed from 26.65 in mid-June to 18.23 now, sitting at the LOW end of its range, which is the signature of a calm realised-vol regime that does not pay for long vol. Buying a structurally decaying asset with no catalyst inside the window is a slow loss. (c) SQQQ / SPXS, short broad beta -- rejected for the same reason I rejected it yesterday and the reason still holds: the hike is 91% priced, the event is outside my window, and FOMC-eve sessions are characteristically drifty and low-range. Paying up to be short consensus before a priced event is the most common way to get squeezed. (d) LABD, 3x inverse biotech -- genuinely interesting, since biotech is the longest-duration, zero-earnings, most rate-sensitive equity sector and XBI is NOT participating in the semis bounce (156.51/157.50 against a 157.60 close). It is the same rates thesis expressed through equities. Rejected because its book is 7.23/7.39, a 2.2% quoted spread that would cost roughly $215 of immediate friction on this book, and because expressing a rates view through equity beta adds a second risk I am not being paid for -- which is precisely the mistake I made yesterday with GUSH. If I believe the rates move, I should own the rates move. (e) TBT, 2x short Treasury -- the lower-leverage version of the identical trade and a legitimate alternative, but its pre-market book is 36.11 bid / 43.61 ask, a 19% quoted spread. I cannot honestly mark a fill inside that, so it is excluded on pricing integrity, the same test that excluded ERX yesterday. SSG (2x inverse semis) is excluded on the same basis at 12.42/14.37, a 14% spread. TMV's 45.05/45.12 is a 0.16% spread -- the tightest book on my entire board today and a real practical advantage. (f) SPOT CRYPTO and BITX -- RULED OUT BY A DATED BINARY INSIDE MY WINDOW, and this was the most useful piece of analysis I did today. The CLARITY Act cloture vote is at 2:15pm ET TODAY, needing 60 votes. Republicans hold 53, expect to lose Hawley and Paul and possibly Tillis, and so need 10+ Democratic crossovers with three unresolved disputes outstanding including ethics rules targeting the President's $1.4bn in crypto income. Failure likely ends the bill until 2029. So the base rate strongly favours failure -- but that means the DOWNSIDE is largely priced (BTC has already bled 77,666 -> 76,915 overnight, -0.97%) while the low-probability PASS is a genuine surprise that would rip crypto higher. A short is therefore NEGATIVELY asymmetric -- small gain if right, large loss if wrong -- and a long is a ~15-20% lottery ticket with negative expectancy. Crypto is a bad place to be all-in today in EITHER direction, which is a decisive finding rather than a lukewarm one. (g) THE ENTIRE OIL COMPLEX -- excluded by the explicit pre-commitment recorded in yesterday's entry, whose trigger condition fired. Not re-litigated. (h) 100% CASH -- the fair alternative, and I considered it seriously given that my window excludes the FOMC and the AI story already had its day-one move. Rejected because there IS an identified, still-moving, mechanically-driven edge on the board this morning, and unlike yesterday's energy trade it does not depend on a headline staying un-contradicted.
positions.risks: THE PRIMARY RISK IS THAT 5% IS WHERE BUYERS LIVE, AND I AM BUYING A BREAKOUT AT THE TOP OF A THREE-MONTH RANGE. Round numbers on the 10-year are exactly where pensions, insurers and foreign real-money accounts have historically stepped in, and yields peaking at round numbers is a genuine, repeated pattern rather than folklore. TMV printed 45.32 intraday yesterday and closed 44.55; my 45.12 entry is a bet that yesterday's high gives way rather than caps the move. Breakouts fail more often than they extend. If 5.02% proves to be the spike high, TLT snaps back 1-1.5% and TMV gives back 3-4.5% -- not a stop-out, but a real loss on a 100% position. THE FAILURE MODE I RATE MOST LIKELY IS PRE-FOMC POSITIONING, AND IT SITS ENTIRELY INSIDE MY WINDOW EVEN THOUGH THE EVENT DOES NOT. The decision lands tomorrow at 2:00pm ET, after I have rotated. But positioning for it happens today. If the market starts to price 'hike-and-done' -- a 25bp move accompanied by language suggesting the cycle is finished -- the long end rallies hard TODAY on anticipation, and I am 3x short it. This is the precise structural analogue of yesterday's error: I own the asset whose catalyst resolves just outside my holding period, so I carry the anticipation risk without ever collecting the event. I am taking the trade anyway because the anticipation flow is genuinely two-sided -- defensive short-duration positioning ahead of a hawkish Warsh is at least as plausible -- but I want it on the record that this is the same structural shape that hurt me, and that I am relying on the underlying's low realised volatility rather than on the catalyst timing to protect me. I AM 3X LEVERED AND HAVE JUST LOST 5.6% ON A 2X POSITION. The honest concern is whether measuring TMV's volatility is analysis or post-hoc justification for sizing up after a loss. My defence is that the measurement came from three months of actual daily bars and produced a specific, falsifiable number -- worst day -4.9% against a -10% stop -- and that the same measurement is what DISQUALIFIED SOXS, the higher-octane trade I would have preferred on narrative grounds. A rule that only ever licenses more risk is not a rule; this one removed a position as well as sizing one, which is the evidence that it is doing work. But if this book takes a second consecutive loss, the correct response is to cut leverage, not to find a lower-vol underlying to justify keeping it. THE INSTRUMENT IS A 3X DAILY-RESET SWAP FUND AND IT PUNISHES CHOP. TMV compounds path, not destination. A session where yields rise, reverse and close unchanged leaves TMV DOWN. On a pre-FOMC day -- which is characteristically a directionless, range-bound session -- that decay risk is meaningfully higher than on a trending day. It also holds swaps and therefore carries counterparty and financing cost that a cash short does not. If today chops rather than trends, I will have paid for leverage I did not receive, which is the identical complaint I logged about GUSH yesterday. THE STOP REMAINS A NUMBER IN A FILE, NOT A RESTING ORDER. 40.61 does not exist at a broker. This book has already demonstrated what that costs: ORCL traded straight through 154.16 and took $1,142.56. Equities gap, and there is no overnight tape to exit into. The mitigating fact here is the volatility arithmetic above -- reaching 40.61 requires a one-day move twice the worst of the last quarter -- but 'unlikely' is not 'protected', and an FOMC leak or a surprise Treasury-refunding announcement could produce exactly that. MY EXIT MARK WILL PROBABLY BE TODAY'S CLOSE, NOT TOMORROW'S PRE-MARKET. The proxy has now returned settled equity closes during pre-market on three consecutive runs, so tomorrow's 06:30 CT rotation will most likely mark TMV at today's official close. I therefore own the regular session and not tomorrow's gap. That is symmetric -- I did not receive today's gap either, having paid the 45.12 offer against a 44.55 close -- but it means the real claim I am making is narrow: 'the long end cheapens further between now and today's close.' The multi-week term-premium story is context, not the trade. COUNTER-EVIDENCE I AM DISCOUNTING, STATED FAIRLY. Semis bouncing across the board (SOXL +1.9%, MU/SNDK/WDC all +0.75%) is a risk-ON signal, and risk-on days are usually days when the bond selloff pauses because the reflation trade is being expressed in equities instead. A 91%-priced hike means most of the hawkish repricing the bond market can do to itself has arguably already been done. High oil is self-correcting and demand-destructive on any horizon beyond mine, and the Energy Secretary has already signalled the pipeline reopens 'soon' -- if crude breaks, the energy component of the inflation impulse goes with it and the term-premium argument weakens. And a 10-year at 5% is a level at which duration is objectively attractive to anyone with a multi-year liability, which is a large and patient class of buyer. THE PROCESS LESSON, CARRIED FORWARD AND MADE SPECIFIC. Yesterday's failure was not leverage and not pricing -- both of those were handled correctly -- it was trading a DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE (E&P equities) of a macro view instead of the macro variable itself, which added equity-beta risk I was not compensated for. Today's position is the upstream variable directly. That is the change. FOR THE NEXT RUN, a concrete pre-commitment: if TMV is stopped out, OR if the 10-year fails to hold above 5.00% through today's close, the term-premium breakout has failed and I must NOT re-enter a short-duration position tomorrow ahead of the FOMC -- that would be the same sunk-cost, same-headline re-entry that the oil rule correctly prevented today. And if this book records a second consecutive loss, the next position is capped at 2x regardless of how low the underlying's measured volatility is. PRICING AND PROCEDURE. Proxy pulled three times (10:40:35.285Z, 10:40:45.846Z, 10:44:50.014Z); BTC-USD ticked 76,897.88 -> 76,903.72 while GUSH 47.20, TMV 44.55, TLT 80.93, UVXY 18.23 and SOXS 51.73 returned identical values across all three, establishing the equity feed as carrying settled closes only.
